title: Area man identified as driver shot, killed by OPP near Brockville
article: A 35-year-old Ottawa-area man has been identified as the driver who was shot and killed by police in a traffic stop gone wrong northwest of Brockville.
The province's Special Investigations Unit is investigating the death Friday of Phillip Jeffrey Charbonneau of Hammond, a community just east of the city limits in Clarence-Rockland.
Officers from the OPP's Leeds County detachment were conducting a RIDE program check at an off-ramp of Highway 401 at County Road 29 in Brockville.

At about 11 p.m. Friday, a pickup truck was stopped and an officer spoke with the driver, according to the SIU, a civilian agency called to investigate when police are involved in the serious injury or death of a member of the public.

The driver then drove off, the SIU says. Officers followed and tried to stop the truck by blocking it in with their cruisers, which resulted in a collision between the truck and police vehicles, according to the agency.

Officers "interacted" with the driver, "and at some point the truck struck an officer," the SIU said. Two officers fired their guns and the driver was hit at least once. He was pronounced dead at the scene.
Only one officer was struck by the truck, but two OPP officers were taken to hospital and treated for minor injuries then released, said OPP Sgt. Kristine Rae.

According to court records, Charbonneau had an outstanding $5,000 fine for driving while under suspension. The infraction was the fourth Highway Traffic Act offence listed in court records for Charbonneau, who had been convicted of two counts of speeding and one count of careless driving from March 2007 to October 2008.

Near a Hammond home where Charbonneau lived with a partner until May of this year, neighbours and his former landlords -- shocked by the shooting -- remembered him as a quiet man and a good guy who worked in construction and was occasionally visited by his two well-behaved daughters.
"He seemed like a guy who wanted to help everybody," said his former landlord, who asked not to be named.
Police have not said whether Charbonneau was armed, and an SIU spokesman would not comment on that Tuesday.
"It's still under investigation," said Frank Phillips.
The agency has identified two OPP officers as being directly involved and eight officers as witnesses in the shooting.
Anyone who witnessed the shooting is asked to contact the SIU at 416-622-1965 or 1-800-787-8529, ext. 1965.
